# KCH Extension Curation

## Native-first ladder

1. Existing host capability.
2. AGENTS or native instruction.
3. Standalone skill.
4. Lifecycle hook or native execution rule.
5. Local function/tool or plugin component.
6. MCP only when the capability depends on an external service or no deeper native path exists.

## Evaluation

For each candidate record source, version, maintenance, permissions, data egress, authentication, platform support, reversibility, update channel, collision risk, cost and evidence. “Found” is not “recommended”; “installed” is not “enabled”; “enabled” is not “authorized”.

## Installation gate

Do not install merely because a candidate ranks first. Present material permissions and side effects, obtain the authority required by the host, install reversibly and run a native smoke test in a new session. Preserve a manifest and uninstall path.

When MCP is selected, document the exact missing native capability that justifies the degradation.
